## Building an AI startup?

You might be eligible for our Startup Program. Get fully funded access to the infrastructure you’re reading about right now (up to $20K value).

All 30 tools are enabled by default. To limit the server to some of them, set `&groups=` or `&tools=` in Remote MCP, or `GROUPS` or `TOOLS` in Local MCP. The group of each tool is listed in the table below.

## Bright Data MCP Tools Reference

| Tool Name | Description | Group |
|---|---|---|
| `search_engine` | Search Bing (default) or Google. Returns JSON organic results (link, title, description), 10 per page. Parameters: `country`, `page` (from 0), `time_range` (`hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`, `any`; Bing supports only `day`, `week` and `year`). | `all` |
| `scrape_as_markdown` | Fetch one web page with Bright Data’s Fetch API. Returns JSON: `url`, `title`, `format`, `content`. Content is Markdown by default; pick `text`, `html` or `ld_json` with the `format` parameter. No JavaScript rendering; pages that take longer than 45 s time out. | `all` |
| `search_engine_batch` | Run up to 5 searches in parallel, with the same parameters as `search_engine`. Returns a JSON array with a result or an error per query. Searches not done within 55 s return a timeout error. | `advanced_scraping` |
| `scrape_batch` | Fetch up to 5 web pages at once with Bright Data’s Fetch API. Returns a JSON array in input order: `url`, `title`, `format`, `content` per page, or `url` and `error` if that page failed. Same `format` parameter as `scrape_as_markdown`. Pages not done within 35 s return a timeout error. | `advanced_scraping` |
| `session_stats` | Report how many times each tool has been called during the current MCP session. | `advanced_scraping` |
| `ask_brightdata_assistant` | Ask Bright Data’s support assistant (Sophie) about Bright Data products, APIs, MCP usage, zones, scraping or account setup. Supports follow-ups via `dialog_id`. | `all` |
| `search_scrapers` | Find a pre-built scraper by site or data type, e.g. “amazon reviews” or “linkedin.com”. Returns `dataset_id`, name, domain and collection methods. | `scrapers` |
| `get_scraper_details` | Show a scraper’s description, input fields, `sample_input` and main output fields for one collection method. Call before `run_scraper`. | `scrapers` |
| `run_scraper` | Run a scraper method on a list of inputs shaped like `sample_input`. Waits up to 45 seconds; if the run is still going, returns a `snapshot_id` with status `running`. Billed per record. | `scrapers` |
| `get_scraper_progress` | Status of a scraper run: starting, running, ready, failed or canceled. | `scrapers` |
| `get_scraper_results` | Records of a finished scraper run. Returns status `running` if the run is not ready yet. | `scrapers` |
| `refresh_scrapers` | Reload the scraper list now instead of waiting for the daily refresh. | `scrapers` |
| `list_dataset_fields` | List the filterable fields of a searchable dataset with each field’s name, type and description. Call before `search_dataset` to learn which fields you can filter on. | `social`, `business` |
| `search_dataset` | Search a Bright Data dataset by a filter and get matching records back directly, with no snapshot step. Finds many records by criteria, unlike `run_scraper`, which collects fresh records by URL. Returns up to 10 records per call with `search_after` pagination. | `social`, `business` |
| `scraping_browser_navigate` | Open or reuse a scraping-browser session and navigate to the provided URL, resetting tracked network requests. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_go_back` | Navigate the active scraping-browser session back to the previous page and report the new URL and title. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_go_forward` | Navigate the active scraping-browser session forward to the next page and report the new URL and title. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_snapshot` | Capture an ARIA snapshot of the current page listing interactive elements and their refs for later ref-based actions. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_click_ref` | Click an element using its ref from the latest ARIA snapshot; requires a ref and human-readable element description. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_type_ref` | Fill an element identified by ref from the ARIA snapshot, optionally pressing Enter to submit after typing. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_fill_form` | Fill several form fields identified by ARIA refs in one call. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_screenshot` | Capture a screenshot of the current page; supports optional full_page mode for full-length images. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_network_requests` | List the network requests recorded since page load with HTTP method, URL, and response status for debugging. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_wait_for_ref` | Wait until an element identified by ARIA ref becomes visible, with an optional timeout in milliseconds. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_get_text` | Return the text content of the current page’s body element. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_get_html` | Return the HTML content of the current page; avoid the full_page option unless head or script tags are required. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_scroll` | Scroll to the bottom of the current page in the scraping-browser session. | `browser` |
| `scraping_browser_scroll_to_ref` | Scroll the page until the element referenced in the ARIA snapshot is in view. | `browser` |
| `chatgpt_ai_insights` | Send a prompt to ChatGPT and get the answer back as Markdown. Useful for GEO and LLM as a judge. | `geo` |
| `perplexity_ai_insights` | Send a prompt to Perplexity and get the answer back as Markdown. Useful for GEO and LLM as a judge. | `geo` |

## How do I get structured data from a site with the Bright Data MCP server?

Use the Scraper API tools to run any of thousands of pre-built scrapers and get structured JSON back. The tools are on by default.

1. Call `search_scrapers` with a site or data type, for example “amazon reviews” or “linkedin.com”. It returns each matching scraper’s `dataset_id` and collection methods.
2. Call `get_scraper_details` with the `dataset_id` and one method. It returns the input fields and a `sample_input`.
3. Call `run_scraper` with an `input` list shaped like `sample_input`. A `collect_by_url` method returns one record per input. A `discover_by_*` method returns up to `limit_per_input` records per input (default 10). Every record is billed.
4. If `run_scraper` returns status `running` after 45 seconds, call `get_scraper_progress` until the run is ready, then call `get_scraper_results`.

Records with an `error` field explain inputs that failed, such as a URL of the wrong type. If a run fails, `scrape_as_markdown` works on the same URL as a fallback.

## How do I search datasets by filter with the Bright Data MCP server?

Use `list_dataset_fields` and `search_dataset` to find many records that match your criteria, as opposed to `run_scraper`, which collects fresh records by URL. The search runs directly against the dataset with no snapshot step and returns up to 10 records per call. Under the hood, `list_dataset_fields` calls the [Get dataset metadata](/api-reference/marketplace-dataset-api/get-dataset-metadata) endpoint and `search_dataset` calls the [Search dataset](/api-reference/marketplace-dataset-api/search-dataset) endpoint of the Marketplace Dataset API. Three datasets are searchable:

| `dataset_id` | Dataset |
|---|---|
| `gd_l1viktl72bvl7bjuj0` | LinkedIn people profiles |
| `gd_me5ppxjr2ge6icjuh0` | LinkedIn people profiles (contact-enriched) |
| `gd_l1vikfnt1wgvvqz95w` | LinkedIn company information |

The workflow is two calls:

1. Call `list_dataset_fields` with a `dataset_id`. It returns each filterable field’s name, type and description.
2. Call `search_dataset` with the same `dataset_id` and a `filter`.

A filter is a tree with a maximum nesting depth of three. Each node is either a group, `{"operator": "and" | "or", "filters": [...]}`, or a leaf, `{"name": ..., "operator": ..., "value": ...}`. See [filter syntax](/api-reference/marketplace-dataset-api/filter-syntax) for the full list of leaf operators and their behavior. For example, this filter matches profiles in the United States whose position mentions data engineering:

```
{
  "operator": "and",
  "filters": [
    { "name": "country_code", "operator": "=", "value": "US" },
    { "name": "position", "operator": "includes", "value": "data engineer" }
  ]
}
```

The response contains `hits` (the matching records), `total_hits` and `took` (search time in milliseconds). To page through more than 10 results, set `sort` to `"default"` or a custom sort like `[{"timestamp": "asc"}]`, then pass the response’s `search_after` cursor into the next call. Set `sort` to `"random"` to sample records instead.
